2608.22138.title: Measuring Stability and Failure Behavior in Language Models Under Structured Perturbations
2608.22138.paper_summary: Language models are usually judged by a single accuracy score, which does not reveal how their performance degrades as inputs are perturbed. We present a graded, multi-family, failure-aware framework for stress-testing reasoning models. It perturbs each problem along a multi-level severity ladder across seven families: six that preserve the answer, paraphrase, input noise, formatting, irrelevant context, context load, and conflicting instructions, and a Knowledge Boundary family that removes answerability so that refusal becomes the correct response. Every test is validity-gated and labeled by its measured severity, and each model is summarized by per-level Accuracy, a magnitude-weighted Stability, and a per-family Collapse Point defined relative to the model's own baseline. Instantiated on the same 100 seed problems used by GSM-Symbolic, expanded into 4,473 gated tests and run on four models spanning capability tiers, the framework exposes structure that an aggregate score hides: the level at which a model fails is family-specific rather than global, and two stressors expose consistent weaknesses across all models: conflicting instructions and questions built on an impossible premise. Recognition of unanswerability is otherwise uneven, reliable on missing information and fabricated evidence but weak on impossible premises. These failure points are invisible to standard accuracy reporting.
2608.22138.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型通常是根據單一的準確度分數來評估的，這並未顯示出當輸入受到擾動時其性能的下降。我們提出了一個分級的、多家族的、失效感知框架，用於壓力測試推理模型。它沿著多級嚴重性梯度擾動每個問題，涵蓋七個家族：六個保留答案的家族，包括改述、輸入噪聲、格式、無關上下文、上下文負荷和衝突指令，以及一個知識邊界家族，該家族移除可回答性，使拒絕成為正確的回應。每個測試都是有效性閘控的，並根據其測得的嚴重性進行標記，每個模型則通過每級準確度、幅度加權的穩定性和相對於模型自身基線的每家族崩潰點進行總結。在使用GSM-Symbolic的相同100個種子問題上實例化，擴展為4,473個閘控測試並在四個跨越能力層級的模型上運行，該框架揭示了總分隱藏的結構：模型失敗的級別是特定於家族的，而非全球性的，兩個壓力源在所有模型中揭示了一致的弱點：衝突指令和建立在不可能前提上的問題。對於無法回答的識別則是參差不齊的，對缺失信息和捏造證據的可靠性較高，但對不可能前提的反應則較弱。這些失效點對標準準確度報告來說是不可見的。
2608.22138.author: Samira Golsefid et.al.
